mainTopic: תרומה for a ארוסה of a כהן according to בן בג בג, and the reason for בית שמאי's דינר minimum for קידושין
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about a בת ישראל betrothed to a כהן: may she eat תרומה before the חופה? רבי יהודה בן בתירא learned from an עבד כנעני that she may by תורה law, but the רבנן stopped her because of עולא's worry that she would share it with her family. The גמרא explains that בן בג בג rejects that comparison, because a slave's sale can never be cancelled for a defect (סימפון), while a woman's קידושין might be. Since both views keep her from eating in practice, the גמרא finds the difference in three cases: קיבל, מסר and הלך, where only one of the two worries applies. Then the גמרא returns to the משנה and asks why בית שמאי require a דינר for קידושין with money. רבי זירא says a woman cares about her dignity, and after אביי's challenge from רבי ינאי's daughters he limits this to cases where she did not see the amount. רב יוסף gives another reason: רב אסי's rule that money in the תורה means valuable צורי coinage. The גמרא then quotes רב אסי's rule on its own and begins to question whether it is really a fixed rule.

steps.title: She does not eat until the חופה, because of עולא's concern
steps.stepSummary: The end of the previous statement: even according to רבי יהודה בן בתירא, the רבנן forbade her from eating until the חופה because of עולא's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until she enters the חופה, because of עולא's reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a thought from just before this piece. Even though she may eat by תורה law, the רבנן stopped her until she enters the חופה, because of the concern raised by עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the whole section. Both opinions end up agreeing that in practice she does not eat before the חופה. רבי יהודה בן בתירא's reason is a rabbinic decree, not the Torah law itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The wedding canopy, the stage of נישואין (full marriage)
Because of

phrases.english: until she enters the wedding canopy,
because of the reason of עולא.
phrases.notes: This points back to עולא's worry from earlier: she might share the תרומה with her non-כהן family.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the statement from the previous part of the daf
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By rabbinic decree she does not eat until the חופה, because of עולא's concern

steps.title: What does בן בג בג do with the slave comparison?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how בן בג בג answers רבי יהודה בן בתירא's קל וחומר from an עבד כנעני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בן בג בג? (How does he get around the קל וחומר?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about בן בג בג. It is setting up the next move, which explains why he does not accept the slave comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר says that if a slave bought with money eats תרומה, a woman acquired with money surely should. The גמרא wants to know what flaw בן בג בג sees in this argument.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stronger one

phrases.english: And בן בג בג?
phrases.notes: He means: what does בן בג בג say about the קל וחומר from the slave?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי יהודה בן בתירא to how בן בג בג handles the קל וחומר
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why בן בג בג does not accept the קל וחומר from the slave

steps.title: There is no cancelling a slave's sale because of a hidden defect
steps.stepSummary: בן בג בג holds that a slave's sale cannot be undone because of a defect. Visible defects were seen, and hidden ones do not matter for work.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not hold that סימפון applies to slaves. If it is a visible blemish, the buyer saw it. If it is a hidden blemish, why should he care? He wants the slave for work, so it does not bother him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בן בג בג holds a slave's purchase can never be cancelled because of a defect (סימפון). It then explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Visible blemishes cannot count, because the buyer saw them and bought anyway. Hidden blemishes cannot count either, because he only wants the slave for labor. So the slave's sale is always firm, while a woman's קידושין could turn out to be a mistake. That is why the slave is no proof for the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: A hidden defect that can cancel a deal after the fact
Visible blemishes
Hidden blemishes
Work, labor

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean slaves have no rules of sale. It only means the purchase of a slave cannot be cancelled because of a defect, unlike קידושין.

phrases.english: He does not hold that a claim of hidden defect applies to slaves.
If it is visible blemishes,
he saw him (and bought him anyway).
If it is because of hidden blemishes,
what difference does it make to him?
He wants him for work;
it does not bother him.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A slave's sale can never be undone through סימפון, so it cannot serve as proof for קידושין, which might be undone
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the קל וחומר breaks down: the slave's acquisition is always secure, but the woman's may not be.

steps.title: Even a thief or a gambler stays sold
steps.stepSummary: Even if the slave turns out to be a thief or a gambler, the sale stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is found to be a thief or a gambler, he is the buyer's (the sale stands).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a rule that backs up the point. Even defects that do affect the slave's usefulness, like stealing or gambling, do not cancel the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that stealing or gambling is a hidden defect that really matters to the buyer. Still, the slave belongs to the buyer. This shows how firm a slave's sale is.

keyTerms.meaning: A thief
A dice player, a gambler
Literally, 'it has reached him': the slave is the buyer's and the sale stands

phrases.english: If he is found to be a thief or a gambler,
he is the buyer's (the sale stands).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 3's point to defects that do affect the slave's usefulness
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave found to be a thief or gambler still belongs to the buyer

steps.title: What about an armed robber or a man wanted by the government?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a stronger case: a slave who is an armed bandit or condemned by the government, who could be taken away and killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What will you say? That he is an armed bandit, or one sentenced by the government? (Surely that should cancel the sale!)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible challenge. This slave could be seized at any time, so surely this defect should cancel the sale. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike stealing, this defect could make the slave worthless, since the government may kill him. So it seems like a real reason to cancel the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: An armed robber
Wanted or sentenced by the government
What will you say? (introduces a possible objection)

phrases.english: What will you say?
That he is an armed bandit
or one sentenced by the government?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is מוכתב. Both mean the same here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an exception to the rule of step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a slave's sale is never cancelled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A slave who may be executed is a defect that should surely let the buyer cancel the sale

steps.title: Those things are public knowledge
steps.stepSummary: An armed robber or a condemned man is known to everyone, so the buyer should have known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these cases make noise; people know about them. So the buyer cannot claim he was fooled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this is public, it is treated like a visible blemish that the buyer knew and accepted. So even this does not cancel the sale. The rule of step 3 stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: They have a 'voice': they are publicly known

steps.whatToRemember: According to בן בג בג, a slave's sale is never cancelled because of a defect. That is why a slave cannot prove anything about a woman's קידושין, which might be cancelled.

phrases.english: Those things are publicly known!

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the case: the defect counts as known, like a visible blemish
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A slave who could be executed is a hidden defect that cancels the sale
steps.terutzMaskana: Such things are publicly known, so the buyer accepted the risk and the sale stands

steps.title: If neither lets her eat, what is the difference?
steps.stepSummary: Since both opinions agree that in practice she does not eat before the חופה, the גמרא asks what difference there is between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, according to both masters she does not eat. So what is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that בן בג בג and רבי יהודה בן בתירא give the same result in practice. It asks what practical difference remains, setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions keep her from eating only because of a rabbinic concern; they differ in which concern. For בן בג בג, the worry is that a hidden defect (סימפון) may later cancel the קידושין. For רבי יהודה בן בתירא, it is עולא's worry that she will share the תרומה with her family (step 1). The גמרא looks for a case where only one of these worries applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (introduces a point both sides agree on)
Both according to one master and according to the other
What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: Now, both according to one master and according to the other master,
she does not eat;
what is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי, בֵּין לְמָר וּבֵין לְמָר לָא אָכְלָה, מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining both opinions, asks what practical difference separates them
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the סימפון concern (בן בג בג) and עולא's concern about sharing תרומה with her family (רבי יהודה בן בתירא) would lead to different results

steps.title: Three cases where the two reasons give different results
steps.stepSummary: The difference between the two reasons shows up in three cases: he accepted her defects, her father handed her over, or the father's agents went with the husband's agents.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a practical difference between them: if he accepted her defects, if her father handed her over, or if her father's people went along with his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 7. It names three cases where the two reasons lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband accepted her defects (קיבל), the fear of a hidden defect (סימפון) is gone, so by בן בג בג she could eat, but עולא's sharing fear remains, so by רבי יהודה בן בתירא she still may not. If she was handed over (מסר) or the agents went together (הלך), she is out of her father's house, so the sharing fear is gone and רבי יהודה בן בתירא would let her eat, but the defect fear remains for בן בג בג.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them in practice
He accepted her defects in advance
Her father handed her over to the husband's agents
The father's agents walked along with the husband's agents

steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons that agree in the normal case can still split apart in special cases. קיבל removes one concern, and מסר or הלך removes the other.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
he accepted, he handed over, and he went.
phrases.notes: These are short code words: he 'accepted' her defects, her father 'handed her over' to the husband's agents, or the father's agents 'went' with the husband's agents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two reasons differ in cases of קיבל (only the sharing concern applies) and מסר or הלך (only the defect concern applies).

steps.title: Why do בית שמאי require a full דינר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about קידושין with money and asks for the reason behind בית שמאי's minimum of a דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: with money, בית שמאי say a דינר, and so on. What is the reasoning of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's rule that בית שמאי need a דינר for קידושין and asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל say a פרוטה is enough. The question is what makes בית שמאי set the minimum so much higher.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי
A silver coin, worth much more than a פרוטה
What is their reason?

phrases.aramaic: בְּכֶסֶף, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים בְּדִינָר וְכו׳.
phrases.english: With money, Beit Shammai say with a dinar, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה. The 'etc.' stands for the rest of it, where בית הלל say a פרוטה is enough.

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Beit Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תרומה discussion and returns to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for בית שמאי's minimum of one דינר for קידושין with money.

steps.title: A woman cares about her dignity
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that a woman is particular about her own honor and would not agree to be betrothed for less than a דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Because a woman is particular about herself, and she does not become betrothed with less than a דינר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question. בית שמאי's rule comes from what a woman would want for herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is not a verse. It is an assumption about her mind: she would feel it is beneath her to be betrothed for a tiny amount. So less than a דינר does not reflect her agreement.

keyTerms.meaning: She is particular about her own honor
With less than a דינר

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira says:
because a woman is particular about herself,
and she does not become betrothed with less than a dinar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא שֶׁכֵּן אִשָּׁה מַקְפֶּדֶת עַל עַצְמָהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A woman cares about her dignity and will not agree to קידושין for less than a דינר.

steps.title: What about the daughters of רבי ינאי?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges: if it depends on her being particular, very proud women would not be betrothed even with a דינר, which seems wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, take רבי ינאי's daughters, who are particular about themselves and would not be betrothed with less than three קבין of דינרים. If one of them reached out and took one זוז from another man, would that also not be קידושין?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבי זירא's reason. He pushes it to an extreme case to show it leads to a strange result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the minimum depends on how particular the woman is, then each woman would have her own minimum. Then a proud woman who willingly takes a דינר would not be betrothed. אביי assumes that is clearly wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (opens a challenge that pushes the idea further)
A measure of three קבין
A זוז, the same value as a דינר

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying רבי ינאי's daughters really need that much money. He is showing that רבי זירא's reason seems to lead there.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: But if that is so,
for example, the daughters of Rabbi Yannai,
who are particular about themselves,
and are not betrothed with less than three kav of dinars,
phrases.notes: A קב is a measure of volume. He means a whole pile of coins, not a counted amount.

phrases.english: so too, if she reached out her hand
and accepted one zuz from another man,
so too, would it not be a betrothal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's reason that the minimum depends on the woman being particular.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the reason, a very proud woman who willingly took a דינר would not be betrothed, which is unreasonable.

steps.title: The rule applies only when she did not choose the amount herself
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that his rule is not about a woman who knowingly accepts. It is about when she was betrothed at night or through an agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did not mean a case where she reached out and accepted. I meant where he betrothed her at night, or where she made an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers אביי by narrowing his rule. A woman who knowingly takes the money has given up her dignity, so it is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being particular only matters when we do not know what she agreed to. At night she cannot see the coin, and an agent was not told the amount. In those cases we assume she wanted at least a דינר. The daughters of רבי ינאי who knowingly take a זוז are betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: I did not say that
At night, when she cannot see what is given
An agent who acts for her

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי זירא, בית שמאי's דינר is a guess about her wishes when she did not see the amount. If she knowingly accepts less, she has agreed.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I did not mean where she reached out her hand and accepted it,
when I spoke, I meant where he betrothed her at night,
or else where she appointed an agent.
phrases.notes: She sent an agent without telling him how much to accept.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule to specific cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי understood the rule to cover every case, even when she knowingly accepts a small amount.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies only when she did not see or set the amount: betrothal at night or through an agent.

steps.title: רב יוסף gives a different reason based on תורה money
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that בית שמאי require a דינר because, according to רב אסי, every mention of money in the תורה means the valuable צורי coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The reason of בית שמאי follows what רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי. For רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: Every money mentioned in the תורה is Tyrian money, and money of the Rabbis is local money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a second answer to the question of why בית שמאי require at least a דינר. Instead of the woman's pride, he points to a rule about how the תורה measures money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a woman is acquired with כסף, money. רב יוסף uses רב אסי's rule that money in the תורה is measured in the strong צורי coinage, where the smallest silver coin is worth a דינר. So for בית שמאי, the minimum is set by the תורה's own standard, not by how the woman feels.

keyTerms.meaning: Their reason
Tyrian money: high-value coins from the city of Tyre
Local or provincial money, worth much less
Amounts set by the Rabbis (rabbinic law)

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not arguing on the הלכה of בית שמאי. Both he and רבי זירא agree they require a דינר. They only disagree about the reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the source of the דינר minimum from the woman's feelings to a fixed תורה measurement, so it would apply even to a woman who agrees to less.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The reason of Beit Shammai
is like what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav Asi.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: For Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav Asi:
Every money mentioned in the Torah –
is Tyrian money,
phrases.notes: Coins from Tyre were worth a lot, so the smallest silver coin in that system is already a דינר.

phrases.english: and money of the Rabbis – is local money.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: טַעְמַיְהוּ דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the question of step 9, replacing רבי זירא's reasoning that was challenged and defended in steps 11-12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי's דינר minimum comes from the rule that money in the תורה is measured in צורי coinage.

steps.title: The גמרא returns to רב אסי's rule on its own
steps.stepSummary: Using the word גופא, the גמרא repeats רב אסי's rule about Torah money so it can examine it directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: Every money mentioned in the תורה is Tyrian money, and money of the Rabbis is local money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now leaves the topic of בית שמאי and quotes רב אסי's rule again by itself. This is a setup line, preparing to question the rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is going to study a statement that was just quoted in passing. The words are the same as before, but now the rule is the main subject instead of a support for בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: the גמרא turns to discuss a statement quoted earlier

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a mistake or a repeat for no reason. The גמרא repeats the rule on purpose because it is about to examine it.

phrases.english: The matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav Asi:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל כֶּסֶף הָאָמוּר בַּתּוֹרָה – כֶּסֶף צוֹרִי,
phrases.english: Every money mentioned in the Torah – is Tyrian money,
and money of the Rabbis – is local money.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule that רב יוסף used as support in step 13 and makes it the new topic of discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורה amounts of money are measured in צורי coinage; rabbinic amounts are measured in local coinage.

steps.title: Is this really a fixed rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב אסי's statement is truly a general principle that holds every time the תורה mentions money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it a general rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אסי's rule by asking whether it can really be a rule for every case. This sets up the discussion on the next amud, where cases that seem not to fit are raised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי said כל, every money in the תורה. The גמרא doubts that such a broad statement can work everywhere, since there may be תורה cases where a smaller amount of money is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule or principle
And is it a rule? A doubting question that challenges a broad statement

phrases.english: And is it a general rule?
phrases.notes: This is a doubting question. The גמרא suspects some תורה cases do not fit רב אסי's word 'every'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the rule just restated in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's claim that every amount of money in the תורה is measured in צורי coinage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A statement using 'every' must hold in all cases; the גמרא suspects there are תורה cases where less money is enough, which would break the rule.
